environment: certification workstation - real PostgreSQL; only the provider and the queue are substituted
command: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run tests/email-send-once-invariant.test.ts tests/email-idempotency.test.ts tests/email-worker.test.ts tests/email-safety.test.ts tests/demo-email-barrier.test.ts tests/sequence-worker.test.ts tests/sequence-execute.test.ts

metrics.whyThatMatters: tests/email-worker.test.ts mocks Prisma entirely, including the outboundMessage.updateMany that IS the compare-and-set the invariant rests on. A mocked CAS cannot prove a CAS. email-send-once-invariant.test.ts runs the real handler against real Postgres and counts entries pushed by the substituted provider, so "sent once" is measured physically rather than logically.
scenariosCovered: ten workers race the same message - exactly one physical send
the same job delivered twice in sequence
the same logical step upserted twice yields one row
ambiguous provider outcome does not re-send
crash between provider acceptance and the status write does not re-send
suppressed recipient never receives, even on a fresh message
a message already marked sent is never re-sent
live claim respected; claim older than the lease is parked; claim with no claimedAt is parked
unsubscribe stops the NEXT step, not only the triggering one
hard bounce stops later steps; soft bounce does not suppress
paused inbox and deactivated sender send nothing, and say why
suppression is matched per tenant, not globally
duplicate webhook: bounce, reply and unsubscribe each applied exactly once across redelivery
reassignment does not duplicate an already-sent message
